_meta: Lead-chasing follow-up round after AF/G.23 (2026-08-13), closing the 'sc-oag-annual-report -> (district/local-government finding)' deferred lead recorded in sc-g23-municipal.json's _dropped block. That prior round reached only the OAG report LISTING page and was blocked from individual report PDFs by an sg-captcha gate on oag.sc. This round found the captcha was not a persistent block: the listing page (https://www.oag.sc/reports/annual-reports-of-the-auditor-general) is now accessible and confirms a full archive of Auditor-General annual reports 2011-2024, each with a direct /download link, and — separately — the individual report PDFs were retrieved cleanly via their National Assembly mirror (nationalassembly.sc), which was never gated. Three consecutive editions (2022, 2023, 2024) were found to track the SAME recurring finding (a 'district small projects' / district-administration budget line administered by the Ministry of Local Government and Community Affairs), which per this branch's convention is modelled as ONE node spanning the three editions rather than one node per exercise-year, with the line item's restructuring between the 2022/2023 and 2024 editions (R20m undifferentiated lump sum -> SR1.0m per district) documented as internal evolution within that node's description rather than split into separate nodes — the underlying subject (a centrally-administered, non-district-controlled district allocation) and the auditing programme (the OAG's annual report) are unchanged across all three editions; only the mechanics of the allocation changed, which is exactly the kind of finding this node exists to preserve rather than a reason to fork the node. This is the THIRD independent primary source in this branch's Seychelles research (alongside sc-constitution-article-167 and sc-mlgii-budget-2026, both in af-seychelles.json / sc-g23-municipal.json) reinforcing the confirmed structural absence of an autonomous local fiscal tier in Seychelles — here from the angle of the national Auditor-General auditing a national ministry's district-facing spending, rather than the constitutional text or the budget document itself. No edge is minted to sc-mlgii-budget-2026: the two documents describe the same general phenomenon (centrally-administered district financing) from different institutional angles, but no textual citation between them was found this round, and the AG reports and the 2026 budget document even name what appear to be two different ministries (Ministry of Local Government and Community Affairs, in the 2022-2024 AG reports, vs Ministry of Local Government and Inner Islands (MLGII), in the 2026 Budget) — recorded as a note rather than force-linked on topical similarity alone, per instruction.

reports.title: Annual Reports of the Auditor-General (Seychelles), 2022-2024 editions — District Small Projects / District Administration Budget Line
reports.publisher: Office of the Auditor-General, Republic of Seychelles
reports.description: Three consecutive annual editions of the Office of the Auditor-General's (OAG) statutory report to the National Assembly, tracking the same recurring line item — a centrally-administered budget allocation for 'district small projects' / district administration, run by the Ministry of Local Government and Community Affairs — across the 2022, 2023 and 2024 reports. 2022 report (Chapter 2, para 2.44, with Ministry response at 2.46): "A budget of R20.0m was allocated for small projects implemented at district level against an actual spending of R12.2m." Ministry response: "The Ministry noted that at the time of budget finalization, the list of projects under the district small projects program is not finalized. The list is only finalized after discussions at the district levels, the result of which is consolidated by the Ministry of Local Government and Community Affairs." 2023 report (Chapter 2, para 2.41), the OAG's own status-tracking cross-reference to the same line: "Lump sum budget of R20m for small projects implemented at district levels without details." This is the third consecutive year (2022, 2023, 2024) this specific line item has been tracked by the AG. 2024 report (Chapter 4 introduction, describing the Ministry's mandate): "The Ministry of Local Government and Community Affairs is mandated to oversee the affairs of the 27 districts and empower the local communities. Its role is to deliver transparent, accountable and inclusive local services; provides and enhance community infrastructure and facilities, implement the local government reform programme and ensure good governance through citizen's engagement, inclusiveness and empowerment towards development." 2024 report (Chapter 2, para 2.44), documenting a restructuring of the same line item away from the prior years' undifferentiated lump sum: "A budget of SR1.0m is now allocated to each of the 26 districts." SOURCE-INTERNAL DISCREPANCY, flagged rather than resolved: the 2024 report itself states "27 districts" in its Chapter 4 introduction and "26 districts" in its Chapter 2 budget-line paragraph — both quoted verbatim as printed in the same document edition. The restructuring documented between the 2022/2023 editions (a single undifferentiated R20m lump sum, unallocated by district, with the OAG repeatedly noting the absence of a finalized project list at budget time) and the 2024 edition (a fixed SR1.0m allocated to each of the 26/27 districts individually) reinforces, rather than weakens, this branch's confirmed finding of a structural absence of an autonomous local fiscal tier in Seychelles: in both the pre- and post-restructuring form, the allocation is set, administered and consolidated centrally by the Ministry, not raised or controlled by the districts themselves — this is the THIRD independent primary source (after sc-constitution-article-167 and sc-mlgii-budget-2026) making that same point, this time from the angle of the national Auditor-General's audit of the national ministry's district-facing spending rather than from constitutional text or the budget document itself. The 2024 report also documents two named audit findings against the same Ministry in the same chapter: absence of alternative quotes obtained for air ticket purchases (SR227,539) and absence of valid procurement contracts for disaster relief meal provisions (SR608,935, described as a recurring issue). The 2020 report (a fourth edition checked this round) returned zero hits for "district" on a full-text search and appears to predate or not cover this line item — a genuine NOT FOUND for that specific document/year, not an access failure (see _dropped).
reports.cadence_note: Annual statutory report to the National Assembly; this node spans three consecutive editions (2022, 2023, 2024) tracking one recurring line item rather than minting a node per exercise-year, per this branch's convention for a finding unchanged in substance across editions.

_dropped.why: Both documents describe the same underlying phenomenon — centrally-administered, non-district-controlled district financing in Seychelles — but from different institutional angles (an Auditor-General audit of a ministry's spending vs. the Ministry of Finance's own budget estimates), and no textual citation of one document by the other was found this round. Not minted as a live edge on topical similarity alone, per instruction. Worth separately flagging: the three AG report editions (2022-2024) name the responsible body as the 'Ministry of Local Government and Community Affairs', while the 2026 Budget Estimates document names it the 'Ministry of Local Government and Inner Islands' (MLGII) — either a ministry rename/reorganisation between the audited years and the 2026 budget, or an inconsistency in how the two document series refer to the same body. Not resolved this round; recorded as a note for a future session rather than assumed to be the same entity without confirmation.

The `sg-captcha` bot-protection gate on oag.sc that blocked the prior round (AF/G.23, recorded in sc-g23-municipal.json's _dropped block) from reaching individual report PDFs appears to have been specific to that round's browser-rendered/direct fetch of the listing page, not a persistent block on the domain. This round, the listing page itself (https://www.oag.sc/reports/annual-reports-of-the-auditor-general) was reached cleanly and confirms a full archive of Auditor-General annual reports 2011-2024, each with a direct /download link; separately, and more productively, the individual report PDFs were retrieved without any gate via their National Assembly mirror (nationalassembly.sc/sites/default/files/...), which was never gated in either round. Worth remembering for future Seychelles research: prefer the nationalassembly.sc mirror for OAG report PDFs over a direct oag.sc fetch, and treat a captcha hit on oag.sc as possibly transient rather than a dead end.

The AG Report 2020 (https://www.nationalassembly.sc/sites/default/files/2021-11/OAG%202020%20Report.pdf) was checked this round for the same 'district small projects' line item tracked in the 2022-2024 editions. A full-text search for "district" returned zero hits. This appears to be a genuine NOT FOUND — the line item either predates this document or is not covered by it — rather than an access or extraction failure; no node or edge is minted for the 2020 edition on this basis.
